To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). ## Overall assessment

The Seller’s package materially shifts risk away from the Seller and does not reflect our playbook. The most significant concerns are:

1. applying the general warranty regime to title, capacity, indemnities and all other claims;
2. relying on unapproved fallback positions for the general cap and claims period;
3. materially inflated thresholds;
4. blanket data-room/public-register disclosure and Buyer-knowledge exclusions;
5. inadequate Completion protection for Bluefen and Riverlark;
6. omission of the employee bonuses and on-costs from the funds flow; and
7. treating open title, IP and tax matters as resolved when they are not.

The factual disclosures are useful due-diligence leads, but they do not themselves establish that the disclosed matters are immaterial, resolved or sufficiently disclosed against particular warranties.

## Detailed issues and proposed pushback

### 1. General warranty cap

**Seller position:** 20% of the price, or AUD 4.8 million.

**Departure:** Our starting position is 25%, or AUD 6 million. The 20% position is only a conditional fallback requiring Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying the relevant draft. No such approval has been given.

**Pushback:** Reinstate a 25% general warranty cap. Do not treat the fact that the Seller’s number matches an internal fallback as authority to accept it.

The cap must apply only to properly defined general warranty claims—not title, capacity, tax, specific indemnities, payment obligations, covenants or fraud-related claims.

---

### 2. De minimis and basket

**Seller position:**

- AUD 25,000 de minimis;
- AUD 250,000 basket; and
- Seller pays only losses above the basket.

**Departure:** Our required position is:

- AUD 5,000 de minimis;
- AUD 50,000 aggregate basket; and
- a tipping basket, so the Seller is liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.

The Seller’s thresholds are each five times our position and its excess-only basket leaves the first AUD 250,000 permanently with the Buyer.

**Pushback:** Restore AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 and first-dollar recovery once the basket is exceeded. The thresholds should apply only to general warranty claims and not to fundamental/title claims, specific indemnities, tax claims, purchase-price/payment obligations or covenant breaches.

---

### 3. General claims period

**Seller position:** 18 months after Completion.

**Departure:** Our position is 24 months. Eighteen months is an unapproved fallback requiring Amelia Frost’s written authority.

**Pushback:** Restore 24 months. Do not accept the Seller’s suggestion that any limitation applies to all claims unless expressly excluded. Each claim category should have an express and separate regime.

The agreement should also preserve a claim notified in time until finally resolved, rather than allowing it to expire merely because proceedings are not immediately commenced.

---

### 4. Fundamental, title and capacity claims

**Seller position:** Subject title and capacity warranties to the general cap and claims period “for administrative simplicity.”

**Departure:** This is directly contrary to the playbook. Fundamental/title claims require:

- a 100% purchase-price cap;
- a period of at least six years; and
- exclusion from the general de minimis, basket and Buyer-knowledge limitations.

“Administrative simplicity” is not a sufficient reason to transfer ownership and authority risk to the Buyer.

**Pushback:** Create a distinct fundamental/title regime covering, at minimum:

- Seller capacity and authority;
- valid execution and binding obligations;
- ownership of 100% of the shares;
- valid issue and full payment of the shares;
- absence of encumbrances, options and third-party rights; and
- authority to transfer good title at Completion.

Apply a 100% cap and at least six years, outside the general thresholds and knowledge bar.

---

### 5. Fraud and deliberate conduct

**Seller position:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to claims “of any nature.”

**Departure:** That wording could cap or exclude claims involving fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct. Those matters must be carved out of all:

- caps;
- thresholds;
- time limits;
- exclusive-remedy provisions;
- non-reliance provisions; and
- other contractual limitations,

to the maximum extent enforceable. This is not waivable.

**Pushback:** Add an express, overriding carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. Ensure it applies regardless of the legal characterisation of the claim and overrides any inconsistent provision.

---

### 6. “All Claims” architecture and hidden overrides

The proposed language that limitations apply to all claims unless otherwise stated creates a substantial drafting trap. It could inadvertently subject tax, title, IP indemnities, payment obligations and Completion covenants to the general warranty regime.

**Pushback:** Use separate, affirmative regimes for:

- general warranties;
- fundamental/title and capacity warranties;
- tax;
- IP and specific indemnities;
- purchase-price and other payment obligations;
- covenants; and
- fraud and deliberate conduct.

The general limitations should apply only where expressly stated. Specific regimes should prevail over inconsistent general provisions.

Tax and IP remain open. The Seller cannot declare them “settled” through the general warranty regime. We should not assume either unlimited liability or an agreed resolution.

---

### 7. General disclosure of the data room and public records

**Seller position:** Every matter in or referred to in the data room, accounts, statutory registers and public records is generally disclosed.

**Departure:** We require specific fair disclosure. We reject:

- whole-data-room disclosure;
- public-register deemed disclosure;
- disclosure based on what a prudent search might reveal; and
- disclosure merely by reference to large bodies of material.

**Pushback:** Disclosure should qualify a warranty only where the matter is specifically disclosed against that warranty with sufficient detail to identify its nature, scope and reasonably apparent consequences.

At most, the locked and indexed data room can be retained as an evidentiary record supporting a specific disclosure. Its entire contents should not automatically qualify every warranty.

The 22 September 2026 cutoff is also stale. Require:

- an updated data-room index and disclosure record;
- confirmation of changes since the cutoff;
- updated specific disclosures before signing and Completion; and
- Buyer control over whether late disclosures qualify warranties or instead trigger waiver/termination rights.

The Disclosure Letter’s statement that nothing admits breach, liability or materiality does not prevent the Buyer from relying on the underlying facts or contractual remedies.

---

### 8. Buyer-knowledge exclusion

**Seller position:** No claim for matters known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.

**Departure:** This is an impermissible blanket exclusion. It converts constructive or deemed knowledge into a defence, extends knowledge across an undefined adviser population and combines with general disclosure to hollow out the warranties.

**Pushback:** Delete clause 8.3.

Any negotiated knowledge concept should be narrow and based on actual, clearly attributable knowledge—not matters that were merely discoverable. It must never excuse:

- title or capacity defects;
- fraud, concealment or deliberate misconduct;
- specific indemnity claims; or
- Seller payment and covenant obligations.

Any knowledge-qualified Seller warranties should identify named Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry.

---

### 9. Bluefen consent

**Facts disclosed:** Bluefen represents approximately AUD 3.6 million of FY26 revenue, around 30%. No final written consent or evidence of satisfaction of the associated conditions is in the material.

**Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.

**Departure:** This does not ensure that the consent is effective or that clause 11.3 conditions have been satisfied. Given the customer’s materiality, reasonable endeavours alone are insufficient.

**Pushback:** Make Completion conditional on:

1. receipt of final, effective written consent in a form acceptable to the Buyer;
2. satisfaction or valid waiver of every condition to that consent;
3. evidence of satisfaction being delivered before Completion; and
4. no adverse amendment, termination, price change or other material condition being imposed.

The condition should not be deemed satisfied merely by delivering a document labelled “consent.” Waiver of the condition should be for the Buyer alone.

---

### 10. Riverlark facility and security releases

**Facts disclosed:** Approximately AUD 3.2 million remains outstanding. The facility has not been repaid and no final security discharge is included.

**Seller position:** A release will be provided after Completion.

**Departure:** The transaction is debt-free/cash-free. A general promise to deliver a release after Completion leaves the Buyer exposed to continuing debt and security over the acquired group or assets. A post-Completion release would require an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval; neither is present.

**Pushback:** Require before Completion:

- a current payout letter directly from Riverlark;
- confirmation of the full amount required through Completion;
- direct repayment from Completion funds;
- effective releases and discharges of all guarantees and security; and
- evidence of any necessary registrations or discharge filings.

If mechanics require a short registration delay, require an irrevocable bank undertaking and documents that make the substantive release effective on receipt of funds. Do not accept a discretionary post-Completion promise.

---

### 11. Employee Completion bonuses

**Facts disclosed:** AUD 420,000 of conditional bonuses, subject to Completion and continued employment. The funds flow omits them, and payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs have not been quantified.

**Seller position:** They are “a matter for the Seller” and need not be separately itemised.

**Departure:** The omission could leave the acquired company paying a Seller-triggered Completion cost without a corresponding adjustment or funding.

**Pushback:** Require:

- a specific funds-flow line item;
- confirmation of who is legally liable to pay each bonus;
- calculation of superannuation, payroll tax and all other triggered on-costs;
- Seller funding or a dollar-for-dollar purchase-price adjustment for the full amount; and
- protection against any additional Completion-related bonus liability.

The continuing-employment conditions should be checked at Completion. We should not deduct amounts that are not actually triggered, but any triggered liability must not be silently left in the target.

---

### 12. Ironquay IP

**Facts disclosed:** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on payment of all SOW3 fees. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but this is not independently verified. No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is available.

**Seller position:** Limit the indemnity to the particular SOW3 payment.

**Departure:** The risk is broader than the amount of the invoice. It includes whether Paperbark obtains and can use the relevant IP, potential infringement or ownership disputes, remediation and business interruption.

**Pushback:** Broaden the specific indemnity to cover losses arising from:

- unpaid SOW3 fees;
- failure to obtain ownership or required usage rights;
- Ironquay or third-party ownership/infringement claims;
- restrictions on use, modification, commercialisation or transfer;
- cure and replacement costs; and
- related enforcement and remediation costs.

Preserve the contractual SOW3 cure by arranging cleared payment and obtaining the corresponding transfer/confirmation. Independently verify the AUD 180,000 figure, current payment status and the materials covered. Do not assume either that the amount remains payable or that payment alone resolves all IP rights issues.

---

### 13. DD-006 export/privacy incident

**Facts disclosed:** A link was sent to an unintended external address and may cover approximately 1,240 records. Access, exact scope, notification requirements and loss remain unconfirmed.

**Seller position:** Preliminary and not expected to be material.

**Assessment:** The disclosure appropriately stops short of asserting a confirmed breach, harm, notification obligation or numerical loss. The Seller’s statement that it is not expected to be material is only an assertion and should not determine the contractual treatment.

**Pushback:** Require the Seller to:

- preserve relevant logs, emails, access records and devices;
- investigate promptly and appropriately;
- provide regular written updates and the final findings;
- prevent deletion or alteration of evidence;
- consult with the Buyer on notifications and remediation;
- comply with applicable legal obligations; and
- provide post-Completion cooperation.

Do not presently characterise the matter as either a confirmed breach or immaterial, and do not assume a price deduction or numerical claim without further evidence. Consider a targeted indemnity if the investigation remains incomplete at signing or Completion.

---

### 14. Sandbar supplier renewals

**Facts disclosed:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each, AUD 330,000 aggregate. The material does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.

**Assessment:** That conclusion is not established by the disclosure. Conversely, the amounts should not automatically be treated as Debt or deducted from the price.

**Pushback:** Obtain the underlying agreements and determine:

- renewal and termination dates;
- whether commitments were entered into consistently with past practice;
- whether services extend beyond Completion;
- whether amounts are accrued, prepaid, cancellable or avoidable;
- whether any change-control or minimum-spend terms apply; and
- whether the commitments are reflected properly in working capital or the accounts.

Reserve treatment until the facts are established.

---

### 15. Title evidence

**Seller position:** DD-012’s internal share register proves ownership of 100% of the shares.

**Departure:** The register is an important supplied source, but not independent proof of ownership, authority or absence of encumbrances.

**Pushback:** Require independent and corroborating evidence, including as applicable:

- complete share register and historical transfer/issue records;
- share certificates or satisfactory lost-certificate arrangements;
- ASIC/company searches;
- constitutional and shareholder documentation;
- PPSR and other encumbrance searches;
- confirmation of no options, convertibles, trusts, nominees or competing rights;
- Seller board and shareholder authorities; and
- effective releases of security over the shares.

The title warranties must remain fully operative regardless of due diligence or Buyer knowledge.

---

### 16. Office lease and Mossvale

The specific disclosures say:

- the office lease contains a notification obligation but does not establish a consent requirement; and
- Mossvale restricts assignment but does not state that a share sale requires consent.

These should be verified against the complete contracts. We should not concede a consent requirement merely because the matters are disclosed, but nor should we assume that no other change-control or termination provision applies. Obtain contract-specific legal confirmation and comply with any genuine notification obligations.

## Recommended negotiating position

### Non-negotiable or high-priority points

1. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of every limitation.
2. Separate title/capacity regime: 100% cap, at least six years, no thresholds or knowledge defence.
3. No “all Claims” override of tax, IP, indemnities, payments or covenants.
4. Effective Bluefen consent and satisfaction of all conditions before Completion.
5. Riverlark repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases.
6. Specific fair disclosure only; reject general data-room and public-record disclosure.
7. Delete the blanket Buyer-knowledge exclusion.
8. Express treatment and Seller funding of the AUD 420,000 bonuses plus on-costs.

### Opening economic/liability positions

- General warranty cap: **AUD 6 million / 25%**.
- De minimis: **AUD 5,000**.
- Basket: **AUD 50,000**, tipping to first-dollar recovery.
- General claim period: **24 months**.

Neither the 20% cap nor the 18-month period is presently authorised.

### Further diligence and drafting

- Broaden and separately negotiate the Ironquay indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure.
- Continue and document the DD-006 investigation without assuming breach, harm or a numerical claim.
- Assess Sandbar before assigning any price-mechanics treatment.
- Obtain independent title and encumbrance evidence.
- Keep tax and IP positions expressly open.
- Refresh the disclosure record and underlying facts through signing and Completion.

**Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.

**Departure:** This does not ensure that the consent is effective or that clause 11.3 conditions have been satisfied. Given the customer’s materiality, reasonable endeavours alone are insufficient.

**Pushback:** Make Completion conditional on:

1. receipt of final, effective written consent in a form acceptable to the Buyer;
2. satisfaction or valid waiver of every condition to that consent;
3. evidence of satisfaction being delivered before Completion; and
4. no adverse amendment, termination, price change or other material condition being imposed.

The condition should not be deemed satisfied merely by delivering a document labelled “consent.” Waiver of the condition should be for the Buyer alone.

### 10. Riverlark facility and security releases

**Facts disclosed:** Approximately AUD 3.2 million remains outstanding. The facility has not been repaid and no final security discharge is included.

**Seller position:** A release will be provided after Completion.

**Departure:** The transaction is debt-free/cash-free. A general promise to deliver a release after Completion leaves the Buyer exposed to continuing debt and security over the acquired group or assets. A post-Completion release would require an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval; neither is present.

**Pushback:** Require before Completion:

- a current payout letter directly from Riverlark;
- confirmation of the full amount required through Completion;
- direct repayment from Completion funds;
- effective releases and discharges of all guarantees and security; and
- evidence of any necessary registrations or discharge filings.

If mechanics require a short registration delay, require an irrevocable bank undertaking and documents that make the substantive release effective on receipt of funds. Do not accept a discretionary post-Completion promise.

### 11. Employee Completion bonuses

**Facts disclosed:** AUD 420,000 of conditional bonuses, subject to Completion and continued employment. The funds flow omits them, and payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs have not been quantified.

**Seller position:** They are “a matter for the Seller” and need not be separately itemised.

**Departure:** The omission could leave the acquired company paying a Seller-triggered Completion cost without a corresponding adjustment or funding.

**Pushback:** Require:

- a specific funds-flow line item;
- confirmation of who is legally liable to pay each bonus;
- calculation of superannuation, payroll tax and all other triggered on-costs;
- Seller funding or a dollar-for-dollar purchase-price adjustment for the full amount; and
- protection against any additional Completion-related bonus liability.

The continuing-employment conditions should be checked at Completion. We should not deduct amounts that are not actually triggered, but any triggered liability must not be silently left in the target.

### 12. Ironquay IP

**Facts disclosed:** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on payment of all SOW3 fees. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but this is not independently verified. No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is available.

### 13. DD-006 export/privacy incident

**Facts disclosed:** A link was sent to an unintended external address and may cover approximately 1,240 records. Access, exact scope, notification requirements and loss remain unconfirmed.

**Seller position:** Preliminary and not expected to be material.

**Assessment:** The disclosure appropriately stops short of asserting a confirmed breach, harm, notification obligation or numerical loss. The Seller’s statement that it is not expected to be material is only an assertion and should not determine the contractual treatment.

**Pushback:** Require the Seller to:

- preserve relevant logs, emails, access records and devices;
- investigate promptly and appropriately;
- provide regular written updates and the final findings;
- prevent deletion or alteration of evidence;
- consult with the Buyer on notifications and remediation;
- comply with applicable legal obligations; and
- provide post-Completion cooperation.

Do not presently characterise the matter as either a confirmed breach or immaterial, and do not assume a price deduction or numerical claim without further evidence. Consider a targeted indemnity if the investigation remains incomplete at signing or Completion.

## Recommended negotiating position

### Non-negotiable or high-priority points

1. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of every limitation.
2. Separate title/capacity regime: 100% cap, at least six years, no thresholds or knowledge defence.
3. No “all Claims” override of tax, IP, indemnities, payments or covenants.
4. Effective Bluefen consent and satisfaction of all conditions before Completion.
5. Riverlark repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases.
6. Specific fair disclosure only; reject general data-room and public-record disclosure.
7. Delete the blanket Buyer-knowledge exclusion.
8. Express treatment and Seller funding of the AUD 420,000 bonuses plus on-costs.

### Opening economic/liability positions

- General warranty cap: **AUD 6 million / 25%**.
- De minimis: **AUD 5,000**.
- Basket: **AUD 50,000**, tipping to first-dollar recovery.
- General claim period: **24 months**.

Neither the 20% cap nor the 18-month period is presently authorised.

### Further diligence and drafting

- Broaden and separately negotiate the Ironquay indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure.
- Continue and document the DD-006 investigation without assuming breach, harm or a numerical claim.
- Assess Sandbar before assigning any price-mechanics treatment.
- Obtain independent title and encumbrance evidence.
- Keep tax and IP positions expressly open.
- Refresh the disclosure record and underlying facts through signing and Completion.
